heading: Saved data, outgoing calls and types
body: context.repository(EntityClass) offers find(page), save(value) and delete(id). They return limited JSON, not class instances filled with the data. Adapters own parameterized operations, authorization and tenancy (keeping the data of each tenant separate). Request methods return descriptors (objects that describe the request) that contain only query, headers and body. The adapter owns a trusted base origin. A literal path cannot select another authority (another host). Transport requests carry redirect: 'error', credentials: 'omit', a signal, a deadline and a 1 MiB response limit. The adapter must enforce that limit while it reads. There are no automatic retries, and no credentials are added without your code. TypeScript decorators cannot add constructor signatures. So declare fields and use Behaviors.construct(Type, { behaviors: context, ...fields }). The runtime checks that the fields are exactly the required set. Request methods should declare the return type Promise<BehaviorJsonValue>, because decorators cannot change the return types that TypeScript infers. Generated projects include tachyon-behaviors.d.ts, and ty writes .tachyon/types/client/composed.d.ts and .tachyon/types/server/composed.d.ts, so a test or role file uses a composed class such as a service without an import. See the repository's docs/BEHAVIOR_ANNOTATIONS.md for the full adapter contract.
